track_A.name: whole-mask hole semantics alignment
track_A.purpose: Make whole-mask hole counting use the same digital-topology convention as the accepted local guard.

track_B.name: bounded single-anchor subdivision after safe underfill
track_B.purpose: Permit one selectable subanchor while retaining one unedited boundary witness when a cell-feasible single parent anchor was excluded solely by the existing directional limit.
eligibility: interface remains feasible in underfill feedback
parent had exactly one anchor and selection limit zero
subdivision is deterministic, exhaustive, disjoint and 8-connected
new identities require fresh nuclei preflight

separation_invariant: Track B may not be invoked to rescue a topology-failing trial. Track A must first produce a topology-passing underfill under its own versioned semantics; only then may Track B eligibility be evaluated.

local_validation.track_A: 228 tests plus 346 subtests, then 72 tests plus 85 subtests

review_questions: Does the 8-foreground/4-background convention correctly align whole-mask and local-guard hole semantics without changing component semantics?
Is the topology-passing-underfill prerequisite sufficient to prevent the reachable-area mechanism from masking a topology failure?
Does deterministic geodesic bisection preserve the scientific meaning of an unedited boundary witness, or is a minimum physical arc length also required?
Must the two tracks receive separate code identities and separate development executions before any combined candidate is tested?
Are the negative cases sufficient before preparing a development-only manifest?
